summary: This informational document defines the formal URN Namespace Identifier for Entertainment Identifier Registry (EIDR) identifiers, which globally and uniquely identify motion picture and television content. It obsoletes RFC 7302.

plainLanguage.summary: Every movie and show can get its own unique ID number, like a library card for films. This lets those IDs be written in the standard form used for names of things on the internet.

subtitle: Standard URN namespace for unique identifiers of movies and television content.

tldr.problem: Motion pictures and television programs need unique identifiers for cataloging, distribution, and metadata management across the entertainment industry, but these identifiers need to fit into the standard URN (Uniform Resource Name) format used on the internet.
tldr.mechanism: EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry) defines a formal URN namespace that wraps EIDR Identifiers (which are based on DOI Names) into the standard URN format using the namespace identifier 'eidr' and colon separators.
tldr.outcome: Film and television industry participants can now use persistent, globally unique EIDR identifiers in the standard internet URN format. This supersedes RFC 7302 with minor technical updates.

facts.label: Suffix format
facts.value: 5 hex groups of 4 digits plus check character

today: RFC 7972 is an Informational standard that defines the formal URN namespace for EIDR, the Entertainment Identifier Registry. It is the current specification and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: EIDR: Unique IDs for Motion Pictures and TV
sections.content:
RFC 7972 defines the formal URN Namespace Identifier (NID) for EIDR Identifiers, which are globally unique identifiers for motion pictures, television content, and their variants. EIDR Identifiers are centrally registered and bound to metadata describing the associated work at the time of registration.

EIDR Identifiers are a special type of DOI Name (Digital Object Identifier) allocated exclusively to the EIDR Association for audiovisual works. The DOI system provides persistent identification, global uniqueness, and open resolution infrastructure. An EIDR Identifier consists of two parts: a prefix assigned to EIDR Association (currently 10.5240) and a suffix defined by EIDR Association. The canonical representation is 10.5240:7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5, and its URN form is urn:eidr:10.5240:7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5.
sections.plainLanguage: EIDR gives movies and TV shows permanent ID numbers. These numbers are based on a system called DOI that works for any kind of object. This RFC explains how to write EIDR numbers in the standard internet format called URN.

sections.title: URN Syntax and Structure
sections.content:
An EIDR Identifier expressed as a URN, called URN-EIDR, follows the format urn:eidr:EIDR-NSS, where EIDR-NSS (the namespace-specific string) consists of the prefix and suffix separated by a colon. The colon separator is used instead of a slash because slash is a reserved character in URN syntax.

The EIDR-PREFIX is currently always 10.5240, though EIDR Association may introduce additional prefixes in the future. The EIDR-SUFFIX allows characters including letters, digits, hyphens, periods, and underscores. When the prefix is 10.5240, the suffix is further constrained to the RP2079-SUFFIX format specified by SMPTE: five groups of four hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens, followed by a Mod 37,36 check character derived from the ISO 7064 standard.
sections.plainLanguage: The EIDR URN format is like urn:eidr:10.5240:XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-X. The colon separates parts, and the last character is a check digit to catch typing errors.

sections.title: Looking Up and Verifying EIDR Identifiers
sections.content:
As a DOI Name, EIDR Identifiers are resolved by the ISO 26324 Registration Authority, which operates a web service. To resolve an EIDR-NSS, an HTTP GET request is issued to https://doi.org/urn:eidr:... with the full URN-EIDR. If the identifier exists, the service returns an XML document containing metadata associated with the identifier; if not, it returns HTTP 404 Not Found.

The EIDR Association also operates additional services tailored to EIDR users, including registration capabilities and web-based tools. The validity of an EIDR-NSS can only be fully guaranteed by completing the resolution process. For identifiers with the 10.5240 prefix, the check character can be used for local integrity checking.
sections.plainLanguage: To look up an EIDR number, you go to https://doi.org/urn:eidr:... and get back information about the movie or show. The check digit helps catch typing mistakes.

sections.title: Who Registers EIDR Identifiers
sections.content:
The primary registrants of EIDR Identifiers are producers and distributors of audiovisual works, metadata aggregators, and audiovisual archives. Any bona fide member of the motion picture and television industry ecosystem can become an EIDR member and register works. EIDR Identifiers can be used by anyone to unambiguously identify an audiovisual asset and retrieve underlying metadata.

The primary benefits of EIDR are associated with works in wide distribution, management of long or complex distribution chains across multiple territories and platforms, and aggregation of information from multiple sources. EIDR provides a common reference point for the entertainment industry.
sections.plainLanguage: Movie studios, distributors, and libraries can register their films and shows with EIDR. Then anyone can look up the same movie by its EIDR number and know they're talking about the exact same thing.

sections.title: Relation to Previous Standards
sections.content: RFC 7972 obsoletes RFC 7302. The main change is in the resolution process: the RFC was updated to use the HTTPS scheme instead of HTTP and to use the URN-EIDR representation in the resolution URI. This change reflects modern security practices and clearer specification of the identifier form used in the resolution process.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC updates an earlier one (RFC 7302) to use a more secure web connection and clearer instructions for looking up EIDR numbers.

data.title: EIDR URN format
data.code:
Canonical EIDR Identifier:
10.5240/7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5

URN representation:
urn:eidr:10.5240:7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5

Resolution URL:
https://doi.org/urn:eidr:10.5240:7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5
